question.text: 'Godavari Opportunities LVF' is being set up as a Large Value Fund for Accredited Investors. As per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the minimum investment per investor (other than Manager/Sponsor/employees) that qualifies a fund as an LVF?

answer.text: INR 25 crore per investor, and each such investor must be an Accredited Investor
INR 50 crore per investor regardless of accreditation status
INR 1 crore per investor, same as any regular AIF

explanation.text: **The Logic:** As per SEBI (AIF) Regulations (Chapter III provisions on LVF), a Large Value Fund for Accredited Investors is an AIF/scheme where every investor (other than Manager, Sponsor, employees or directors of the Fund/Manager) is an Accredited Investor and invests NOT less than INR 25 crore. LVFs enjoy relaxed limits — e.g., 50% single-investee for Cat I/II (vs 25%), 20% for Cat III (vs 10%), and tenure extension beyond 2 years per fund documents. **The Trap:** Option A (INR 10 cr) is the SSF minimum investment. Option C inflates the number. Option D (INR 1 cr) is the base AIF minimum and does not qualify for LVF relaxations. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A highlights LVF as a high-ticket product segment. XIX-C tests the quantitative threshold and the regulatory-concessions trade-off. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Manager tip: LVF scheme names must end with 'LVF' as per SEBI circular; First Close must be declared within 12 months of registration or PPM filing (whichever is later). Withdrawal of AI consent is NOT permitted for LVF investors — this is a one-way door for LPs once they sign in.
